lesson.text: Quick memory: what is a goal? (Something you can do and see.) Today: goals you can check, steps, and 'When ..., I will ...' plans.
A goal you can check says what, how much and by when: 'Save 300 gold in 3 weeks', not 'get better'.
Split it into steps, in order. Each step is small enough to start today.
An if-then plan picks the moment: 'When I finish a lesson, I put 10 gold aside.' Plans like this make goals much more likely.
Plan for what gets in the way: 'If a friend asks me to play, I say: after my lesson!'
Habits take weeks to stick. One day off hardly matters: just carry on.
Try it in the practice room: put a rocket goal on your Goal Board.

exercises.explain: 'Save 300 gold in 3 weeks' says what, how much and by when.

exercises.prompt: A good plan says when you will do it.

choices: When I finish a lesson, I save 10 gold
exercises.explain: 'When I finish a lesson' is the moment.

exercises.prompt: Missing one day ruins a habit.
exercises.explain: False: one day off hardly matters.

exercises.prompt: Your rocket goal: put the steps in order.
exercises.explain: Learn (it earns gold), save it, buy the parts, build the rocket.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you to play during your plan. Best answer?
exercises.explain: 'After my lesson!' keeps the plan and the fun.

exercises.prompt: You save 10 gold after each lesson. You do 5 lessons. How much gold do you save?
The rocket costs 300 gold. You save 25 a day. How many days?

exercises.hint: Is there a number and a day?
exercises.explain: 2 books by Friday and 50 gold this week can be checked; 'smarter' and 'better' can't.

choices: After I brush my teeth, I read one page
I'll read a lot one day
exercises.hint: Tie it to something you already do.
exercises.explain: Brushing your teeth happens every day: a clear moment.
